# 1 Chronicles Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 381v–382r

---

**1** Then David declared, "This is where the house of the LORD God will stand, and this is where the altar of burnt offering for Israel will be."

**2** David ordered that the foreigners living in Israel be assembled. He appointed stonecutters to quarry and shape the stones for building God's house.

**3** David stockpiled enormous quantities of iron for nails and fittings for the gate doors, and bronze beyond all measuring.

**4** He also gathered cedar logs in quantities too great to count — the people of Sidon and Tyre had shipped vast amounts of cedar to David.

**5** David thought to himself, "My son Solomon is young and untested, and the house to be built for the LORD must be spectacularly great — renowned and glorious throughout the whole world. So I will get things ready for him." And David made extensive preparations before he died.

**6** Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

**7** David told Solomon, "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.

**8** But the LORD's word came to me: 'You have shed too much blood. You have fought too many wars. You will not build a house for my name, because you have spilled so much blood on the ground before me.

**9** But look — a son will be born to you. He will be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. His name will be Solomon — and I will grant peace and tranquility to Israel during his reign.

**10** He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father. I will make his royal throne over Israel stand forever.'

**11** "Now, my son, may the LORD be with you. May you succeed in building the house of the LORD your God, just as he promised you would.

**12** Above all, may the LORD give you wisdom and discernment when he puts you in charge of Israel, so that you may follow the law of the LORD your God.

**13** You will succeed if you carefully follow the decrees and laws the LORD gave Moses for Israel. Be strong and brave! Don't be afraid or discouraged.

**14** I have worked hard to set aside resources for the LORD's house: a hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron too vast to weigh. I have also provided timber and stone, and you can add to what I have gathered.

**15** You have plenty of workers available — stonecutters, masons, woodworkers, and experts in every craft.

**16** You have unlimited gold, silver, bronze, and iron. Now get started! And may the LORD be with you."

**17** David also ordered all of Israel's leaders to support his son Solomon:

**18** "Isn't the LORD your God with you? Hasn't he given you security on every side? He has handed the land's inhabitants over to me, and the land is now under the LORD's control and yours.

**19** Now commit yourselves completely — heart and soul — to seeking the LORD your God. Get to work! Build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that the ark of the LORD's covenant and God's sacred furnishings can be brought into a house built for the LORD's name."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 1 — The declaration:** With a single sentence, David transforms a threshing floor into sacred space. The plague has ended, fire has fallen from heaven, and now David speaks the word that will define Jerusalem's identity for three thousand years: "This is where the house of the LORD God will stand." Every synagogue, church, and mosque in Jerusalem traces its theological geography to this moment.

**Verse 8 — Why David cannot build:** This is the Chronicler's unique contribution to the theology of the temple. David is not punished for his wars — they were divinely sanctioned. But the bloodshed disqualifies him from the sacred work of building. There is a deep logic here: the temple is a house of *shalom*, and it must be built by a man of *shalom*. The play on Solomon's name (*shelomoh* from *shalom*) makes the point unmistakable.

**Verse 14 — "With great effort" or "in my affliction":** The Hebrew *be-onyi* is ambiguous — it can mean "in my poverty/affliction" (ironic, given the vast sums that follow) or "with great effort/toil." Either reading carries weight: David has labored strenuously, or David considers even this enormous treasury to be modest compared to what God deserves.

*— PNEUMA*
